risks: Low: the pathway follows existing guidance; the risk is delayed antibiotics for spreading infection, managed by red flag advice and the safety review.
consent: Allocation is at practice level and outcomes come from routine records; a waiver of individual consent has been requested and the ethics committee has not yet decided. Practices give organisational consent; patients are informed by practice notices and may opt out of data use.
data: Pseudonymised extraction by the network data team; no free text leaves practices except the coding check sample, which stays within the practice.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: people without a regular dentist, in deprived neighbourhoods or with limited English are most affected. Allocation is stratified by deprivation, the triage line offers interpreters, and outcomes are reported by deprivation fifth.
effectiveness: A fall in prescribing without more emergency attendances would justify commissioning the pathway.
efficiency: Uses routine data and an existing dental service.
costs: Triage line staffing is met by the community dental service; data extraction within the data team's role.
grants: A small stewardship grant could fund independent statistical support.
partnerships: Community dental service, microbiology team, local dental committee and a patient panel from the network's participation group.
rebPath: Regional research ethics committee review under ICH-GCP and the Ottawa Statement on cluster trials; the waiver of individual consent is pending, and no allocation happens before the committee decides.
limitations: Few clusters; coded data may miss some consultations; the triage line exists only for 12 months.
summary: Cluster trial with a pending consent-waiver decision, a safety review and equity-stratified allocation.
